chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha', from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whenever Allah intends good for a servant, He grants him understanding in the Religion.

key_terms.الدِّين: The Religion, referring to Islam in its entirety — doctrine, law, and practice
key_terms.خَيْر: Good/goodness; divine favor or blessing in this context
key_terms.فقَّهَهُ: Caused him to have fiqh (deep jurisprudential and practical understanding); from the root f-q-h meaning to grasp deeply

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about God's intention of good for a person and religious understanding?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that divine favor manifests through the gift of deep religious understanding (tafaqquh). This hadith identifies religious knowledge not merely as an intellectual achievement but as a sign of God's particular grace toward a person. The Imam's use of 'faqquhu' — causative form denoting deep, practical comprehension — indicates that understanding in Islam goes beyond memorization to encompass applied wisdom.
word_analysis: causes him to understand/grants him understanding

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Al Washha, from Hammad Bin Usman, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Whenever Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Intends good for a servant, Causes him to have understanding in the Religion’.
en.sarwar: 3. Al-Hassan ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following. “
When Allah wants goodness for a person He gives him (Fiqh) good understanding of religion.”
